units.source_text: 今年的梅雨比往年更多，连日不肯放晴，六条院内诸女眷寂寞无聊，每日晨夕赏玩图画故事。

en.t: This year the plum rains were heavier than usual, and day after day the sky refused to clear; the ladies within the Rokujo estate grew lonely and bored, and morning and evening they amused themselves by looking at illustrated tales.

units.source_text: 明石姬擅长此道，自己画了许多，送到紫姬那里来给小女公子玩赏。

en.t: The Akashi lady was skilled in this art and had painted many pictures herself, which she sent to Lady Murasaki for the little princess to enjoy.

units.source_text: 玉鬘生长乡里，见闻不广，看了更加觉得稀罕，一天到晚忙着阅读及描绘。

en.t: Tamakazura had grown up in the countryside and had not seen much of the world, so she found them all the more marvelous and spent the whole day absorbed in reading and drawing.

units.source_text: 这里有许多青年侍女粗通画道。

en.t: There were many young gentlewomen there who had some modest knowledge of painting.

units.source_text: 玉鬘看了许多书，觉得这里面描写了种种命运奇特的女人，是真是假不得而知，但像她自己那样命苦的人，一个也没有。

en.t: After reading many books, Tamakazura felt that they described all kinds of women with strange fates; whether the stories were true or false she could not know, but not one of them seemed as unfortunate as herself.

units.source_text: 她想象那个住吉姬在世之日，必然是个绝色美人。

en.t: She imagined that the lady of Sumiyoshi, while she lived, must surely have been a peerless beauty.

units.source_text: 现今故事中所传述的，也是一个特别优越的人物。

en.t: Even as she was handed down in the tales of the present day, she was an especially distinguished figure.

units.source_text: 这个人险些儿被那个主计头老翁盗娶，使她联想起筑紫那个可恶的大夫监，而把自己比作住吉姬。

en.t: The fact that this lady had nearly been carried off and married by that old Director of Accounts made Tamakazura think of the hateful assistant governor in Tsukushi, and she compared herself to the lady of Sumiyoshi.

units.source_text: 源氏有时到这里，有时到那里，看见到处都散置着此种图画故事书，有一次对玉鬘说：“啊呀，真讨厌啊！

en.t: Genji went now here, now there, and seeing these illustrated storybooks scattered everywhere, once said to Tamakazura, “Ah, how vexing!

units.source_text: 你们这些女人，不惮烦劳，都是专为受人欺骗而生的。

en.t: You women spare no trouble, as if you had been born solely to be deceived by others.

units.source_text: 这许多故事之中，真实的少得很。

en.t: Among all these stories, very few contain anything true.

units.source_text: 你们明知是假，却真心钻研，甘愿受骗。

en.t: You know they are false, yet you study them earnestly and willingly let yourselves be deceived.

units.source_text: 当此梅雨时节，头发乱了也不顾，只管埋头作画。

en.t: In this rainy season, you do not even mind if your hair grows disheveled, but keep your heads bent over your paintings.

units.source_text: ”说罢笑起来。

en.t: ” Having said this, he laughed.

units.source_text: 既而又改变想法，继续说道：“但也怪你不得。

en.t: Before long he changed his mind and went on, “But I cannot blame you either.

units.source_text: 不看这些故事小说，则日子沉闷，无法消遣。

en.t: If one did not read these tales and romances, the days would be dull, with no way to pass the time.

units.source_text: 而且这些伪造的故事之中，亦颇有富于情味，描写得委婉曲折的地方，仿佛真有其事。

en.t: Moreover, even among these invented stories, there are passages rich in feeling, delicately and intricately described, so that they seem as if they had truly happened.

units.source_text: 所以虽然明知其为无稽之谈，看了却不由你不动心。

en.t: Therefore, even though you know they are groundless tales, when you read them you cannot help being moved.

units.source_text: 例如看到那可怜的住吉姬的忧愁苦闷，便真心地同情她。

en.t: For example, when you read of the sorrow and anguish of that pitiable lady of Sumiyoshi, you sincerely sympathize with her.

units.source_text: 又有一种故事，读时觉得荒诞不经，但因夸张得厉害，令人心惊目眩。

en.t: There are also stories that seem absurd when read, yet because they are so wildly exaggerated, they startle the heart and dazzle the eyes.

units.source_text: 读后冷静地回想起来，虽然觉得岂有此理，但当阅读之时，显然感到兴味。

en.t: Afterward, when you calmly think back on them, they may seem unreasonable, but while you are reading, you plainly feel their fascination.

units.source_text: 近日我那边的侍女们常把古代故事念给那小姑娘听。

en.t: Recently the gentlewomen at my place have often been reading old tales aloud to that little girl.

units.source_text: 我在一旁听听，觉得世间确有善于讲话的人。

en.t: Listening from the side, I feel that there truly are people in this world who know how to tell a story.

units.source_text: 我想这些都是惯于说谎的人信口开河之谈，但也许不是这样吧。”

en.t: I have thought these must all be wild inventions from people accustomed to lying, but perhaps that is not so after all.”

units.source_text: 玉鬘答道：“是呀，像你这样惯于说谎的人，才会作各种各样的解释；像我这种老实人，一向信以为真呢。”

en.t: Tamakazura replied, “Yes, someone used to lying, like you, would be able to offer all sorts of explanations; an honest person like me has always believed them to be true.”

units.source_text: 说着，把砚台推开去。

en.t: As she said this, she pushed the inkstone away.

units.source_text: 源氏说：“那我真是瞎评故事小说了。

en.t: Genji said, “Then I have truly judged tales and romances blindly.

units.source_text: 其实，这些故事小说中，有记述着神代以来世间真实情况的。

en.t: In fact, among these tales and romances there are some that record the true state of the world since the age of the gods.

units.source_text: 像《日本纪》等书，只是其中之一部分。

en.t: Books such as the Nihongi are only one part of them.

units.source_text: 这里面详细记录着世间的重要事情呢。”

en.t: Within them are detailed records of important matters in the world.”

units.source_text: 说着笑起来。

en.t: Saying this, he laughed.

units.source_text: 然后又说：“原来故事小说，虽然并非如实记载某一人的事迹，但不论善恶，都是世间真人真事。

en.t: Then he continued, “After all, tales and romances may not record one person’s deeds exactly as they happened, but whether good or evil, they are all drawn from real people and real events in the world.

units.source_text: 观之不足，听之不足，但觉此种情节不能笼闭在一人心中，必须传告后世之人，于是执笔写作。

en.t: One cannot see or hear enough of such things; feeling that these matters cannot be shut up within one person’s heart and must be passed on to later generations, people take up the brush and write.

units.source_text: 因此欲写一善人时，则专选其人之善事，而突出善的一方；在写恶的一方时，则又专选稀世少见的恶事，使两者互相对比。

en.t: Thus, when wishing to write about a good person, they select only that person’s good deeds and emphasize the good side; when writing the evil side, they choose rare and extraordinary evil deeds, setting the two in contrast.

units.source_text: 这些都是真情实事，并非世外之谈。

en.t: All these are true feelings and real events, not tales from outside the world.

units.source_text: 中国小说与日本小说各异。

en.t: Chinese fiction and Japanese fiction each have their differences.

units.source_text: 同是日本小说，古代与现代亦不相同。

en.t: Even within Japanese fiction, the ancient and the modern are not the same.

units.source_text: 内容之深浅各有差别，若一概指斥为空言，则亦不符事实。

en.t: Their contents vary in depth and shallowness, and to dismiss them all alike as empty words would not accord with the facts.

units.source_text: 佛怀慈悲之心而说的教义之中，也有所谓方便之道。

en.t: Even among the teachings spoken by the Buddha from a heart of compassion, there is what is called the way of expedient means.

units.source_text: 愚昧之人看见两处说法不同，心中便生疑惑。

en.t: Foolish people, seeing two teachings expressed differently, give rise to doubts in their hearts.

units.source_text: 须知《方等经》中，此种方便说教之例甚多。

en.t: You should know that in the Vaipulya Sutras there are many examples of this kind of expedient teaching.

units.source_text: 归根结底，同一旨趣。

en.t: In the final analysis, they return to the same purpose.

units.source_text: 菩提与烦恼的差别，犹如小说中善人与恶人的差别。

en.t: The difference between enlightenment and worldly passions is like the difference between good people and evil people in fiction.

units.source_text: 所以无论何事，从善的方面说来，都不是空洞无益的吧。”

en.t: Therefore, whatever the matter may be, if spoken of from the side of good, it is surely not empty and useless.”

units.source_text: 他极口称赞小说的功能。

en.t: He praised the function of fiction to the utmost.

units.source_text: 接着又说：“可是，这种古代故事之中，描写像我这样老实的痴心人的故事，有没有呢？

en.t: Then he went on, “But among these old tales, is there any story that describes an honest, foolishly devoted man like me?

units.source_text: 再则，这种故事中所描写的非常孤僻的少女之中，像你那样冷酷无情、假装不懂的人，恐怕也没有吧。

en.t: And among the extremely aloof young women described in such tales, there is probably no one as cold and heartless as you, pretending not to understand.

units.source_text: 好，让我来写一部古无前例的小说，传之后世吧。”

en.t: Very well, I shall write a romance without precedent in ancient times and hand it down to later generations.”

units.source_text: 说着，偎傍到玉鬘身边来。

en.t: As he said this, he nestled close beside Tamakazura.

units.source_text: 玉鬘低头不语，后来答道：“即使不写小说，这种古来少有的事情已经传遍世间了。”

en.t: Tamakazura lowered her head and said nothing, but later replied, “Even without writing a novel, this matter, rare since ancient times, has already spread through the world.”

units.source_text: 源氏说：“你也认为古来少有么？

en.t: Genji said, “Do you also think it is rare since ancient times?

units.source_text: 你的态度也是世间无类的呢。”

en.t: Your attitude too is without equal in the world.”

units.source_text: 说着，把身子靠在壁上，情神异常潇洒。

en.t: Saying this, he leaned his body against the wall, his bearing extraordinarily graceful and elegant.

units.source_text: 即席吟诗道：

en.t: On the spot, he composed a poem and said:
